candidates.titulo: Reddit is killing RSS feeds and ending public API access because of AI bots
candidates.resumen: Reddit is ending support for RSS feeds, as the company continues tightening access to its trove of user-generated content.

candidates.titulo: Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post
candidates.resumen:

The company announced Wednesday that its standalone Edits app will now include an AI "creative assistant" that pulls in data from a user's Instagram account and offers suggestions on what to change.

candidates.titulo: DoorDash launches an AI agent you can text to order food
candidates.resumen: By launching an AI agent for food ordering, DoorDash is looking to gain an edge over rivals Uber Eats and Grubhub.

candidates.titulo: All the latest news on Meta’s cute, creepy Muse AI agent
candidates.resumen:
Meta launched a new Muse AI agent it claims can help you with everything from firing off emails to buying stuff online. Muse can be surprisingly effective at delivering on those promises — if you’re willing to trust Meta with your data and hand Muse your credit card. Since the launch, Meta’s also announced plans for a Tamagotchi-like Muse Charm device for its cuddly AI mascot.

candidates.titulo: Google reportedly tests paying publishers for AI search results
candidates.resumen:
Google has launched a pilot program that pays publishers for their contributions to its AI-powered search features, according to a report from The Information. The pilot program reportedly includes around 100 publishers and comes as Google faces scrutiny over the impact of its AI features on web traffic.
